properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 28 at 1:58PM MST until August 31 at 5:00AM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Tucson Metro Area, Southeast Pinal County, Tohono O'odham
Nation, Upper San Pedro River Valley Upper Santa Cruz River
Valley/Altar Valley, Baboquivari Mountains, Catalina and Rincon
Mountains, Dragoon and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita Mountains.

* WHEN...From Saturday morning through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Low-water crossings may be flooded. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An increase in moisture will bring scattered thunderstorms
Saturday and Sunday. Rainfall rates in excess of 1 inch per hour
are expected with the stronger storms with isolated areas having
the potential of 1-3 inches. Additional rainfall from the
previous day and overnight activity will result in faster
responses in normally dry washes, creeks and roadway dips.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM SATURDAY MORNING THROUGH LATE SUNDAY NIGHT

properties.areaDesc: Yellowstone National Park; Absaroka Mountains; Teton and Gros Ventre Mountains; Jackson Hole; Wind River Mountains West; Star Valley; Salt River and Wyoming Ranges
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued August 28 at 10:43AM MDT until August 30 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, northwest, and west central Wyoming,
including the following areas, in central Wyoming, Wind River
Mountains West. In northwest Wyoming, Absaroka Mountains, Jackson
Hole, Teton and Gros Ventre Mountains and Yellowstone National
Park. In west central Wyoming, Salt River and Wyoming Ranges and
Star Valley.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT this evening through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Increased moisture from the Pacific will move across northwest
Wyoming through the weekend, bringing an extended chance for
showers and thunderstorms. The increased moisture will have the
potential to produce locally heavy rainfall, providing excessive
runoff in flood-prone and low-lying areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM MDT THIS EVENING THROUGH SUNDAY MORNING
